title: Priority Stack
hook: When everything feels urgent, nothing important actually gets done.
statement: Not everything is equally important. Rank your priorities and give the top ones your best effort.
explainer: If you treat every task the same, the important stuff gets the same scraps as the trivial stuff. Ranking forces you to put real energy where it pays.
sop: Write down your top 3 priorities this month, ranked.
Rate the Priority of everything on your list from 1 to 10.
Rate your Execution from 1 to 10 on each top 3 item.
Cut or delegate anything below your top 3 that eats real time.
Re-rank weekly. Your number one can change.
equation_example: Priority 9, Execution 3. 9 × 3 = 27 out of 100. Super important, barely getting done. Higher means your big priorities are getting real effort. Lower means you're doing the wrong things well or the right things badly.
question: Write your top 3 priorities for this month from memory. If you can't, that's the problem.
closing_statement: Treat everything as equal and nothing is important.
caption:
Principle Nº 155: Priority Stack

When everything feels urgent, nothing important actually gets done.

Not everything is equally important. Rank your priorities and give the top ones your best effort.

Your turn: Write your top 3 priorities for this month from memory. If you can't, that's the problem.
